purpose: Test Qwen uncertainty-routing, starting with or without one original neighbor on each side; compare against corresponding existing single-pass baselines on all 34 development papers.
stages: First call classifies all frozen NLI candidates as keep/drop/unsure. Second call contains only unsure targets, with up to 3 previous and 3 next original sentences (each <=800 characters); its boolean decision replaces unsure. Other first-pass decisions remain fixed.
first_system:
You are reading sentences from scientific papers. Judge each sentence: does it genuinely state a research gap?

The input is sentences from scientific papers, in reading order, one per line as "[id] sentence". Judge every sentence on its own.

Decision — answer YES (keep) if the sentence states ANY of:
  (a) a limitation / weakness / caveat / bias / constraint / assumption of the authors' OWN work (e.g., small sample, no blinding, single setting, short follow-up, confounding, limited generalizability, unvalidated measure, "we did not / could not ...", "a limitation is ...");
  (b) an explicit FUTURE-WORK direction the authors propose ("in future work we will ...", "future research should ...", "it would be interesting to ...");
  (c) an unsolved problem / missing capability / open research gap in the field or prior work ("it remains unknown ...", "no existing method ...", "current approaches struggle with ...").

Answer NO (drop) if the sentence is instead: a result or finding, a method/experimental-setup description, a positive or contribution claim ("we propose/show/achieve ..."), background or related-work description, a citation or reference fragment, acknowledgements / funding / author contributions / competing interests, a figure or table caption, a dataset/metric definition, or a generic non-gap statement.

Judge each sentence on the rules above, without favouring YES or NO.

Return JSON of the form {"results":[{"id":<id>,"decision":"keep"|"drop"|"unsure"}, ...]} with EXACTLY one entry for every numbered target, using its original id and input order. Use "keep" when the target states a research gap, "drop" when it does not, and "unsure" only when additional original surrounding text is needed to decide reliably. If the available text is sufficient, choose keep or drop. Judge the numbered target itself; any unnumbered neighbors only clarify it.

There are five separate papers below. Lines starting "PAPER " are boundaries, not sentences. Judge each numbered sentence only in its own paper.

Judge each sentence on the rules above, without favouring YES or NO.

Return JSON of the form {"results":[{"id":<id>,"keep":<bool>}, ...]} with EXACTLY one entry for every numbered input candidate, using its original id. Set keep to true for YES and false for NO, in input order.

There are five separate papers below. Lines starting "PAPER " are boundaries, not sentences. Judge each numbered sentence only in its own paper.

The numbered targets were uncertain in a first pass. Use the surrounding original sentences to disambiguate, but decide whether the numbered target itself states a gap. Give a final keep or drop decision for every target.
output_validation: Every target must occur exactly once and have valid decision. Extra out-of-input IDs discarded and recorded; missing, duplicated or conflicting target IDs, truncated output and malformed responses fail.
metrics: Precision, recall and F1 against all labeled sentences; report first-pass unsure counts, final kept counts, Qwen input/output tokens and calls for both passes including retries. No test set or human judgments are used.
caveats: Development papers were previously studied and used in model/prompt selection; labels are LLM-generated, not human-validated. One deterministic run per setup. Different prompts and multi-call costs mean this is exploratory.
